messages:
paul: Heads-up: p95 for route `chat.generate-high-priority` jumped ~18ms after yesterday's kernel switchover. Traces show increased queue wait + KV miss spike.

anya: Which kernel change landed? The mem-prefetch optimizer (opt-mem-prefetch-v2)?

devon: Yep, that one. Rolled at 02:13 UTC. Observed average microbatch size fell from ~6 -> ~4 for this route. KV hit rate also dropped.

rachel: Can you paste the profiler summary (cpu / kernel / io) and a grafana link?

paul: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/XYZ/chat-gen-priority
Profiler run (60s window) snippets:
```
profile summary: p95 latency +18.2ms
kernel time: +4.6ms
queue wait: +9.8ms
kv lookup latency: +2.3ms
kv hit-rate: 78% -> 62% (route-specific cache)
microbatch size: 6.1 -> 4.2
```

paul: The mem-prefetch patch changes ordering of prefetch vs kernel selection; it reduces peak memory but seems to reduce effective KV coalescing for small prefix repeats.

anya: Hypothesis: prefetch shifts KV lookups later so the continuous-batcher sees fewer shared prefixes per microbatch -> smaller microbatches -> higher per-request overhead.

devon: Agreed. Two levers: 1) tweak prefetch ordering, 2) adjust queue policy to bias batch formation for high-tier routes so they get larger microbatches within latency SLO.

rachel: For SLO-driven behavior we should try dynamic token budgets per tier + a gentle queue bias. Proposed quick config:
```
route: chat.generate-high-priority
queue_policy:
  prefer_batching: true
  bias_by_tier: true
dynamic_token_budget_by_tier:
  gold: 1024
  silver: 512
  free: 256
max_microbatch_delay_ms: 8
```

paul: +1 to that config. Add a cap on tokens-per-batch to avoid tail blowups. Also set a canary: 1% of Gold traffic -> apply for 10m -> monitor p95, queue_length, kv_hit_rate.

devon: I'll push a canary via redwoodctl. Command:
```
redwoodctl routes update chat.generate-high-priority --patch-file canary-prefetch.yaml --canary 1%
```

perf-bot: [ALERT] Canary started: chat.generate-high-priority @ 1% at 2294500200 UTC :rocket:

anya: Metrics to watch: p95 (route), microbatch size, kv_hit_rate, kernel_time, queue_wait. Also verify no regression on lower-tier routes.

paul: Important: if kv_hit_rate doesn't improve within 15m, revert prefetch change on canary and try alternate: prefer_prefetch_before_kernel: false (i.e., prefetch earlier).

rachel: Add a lightweight sampling trace to capture prefix overlap per microbatch so we can quantify coalescing. Example: sample 1/1000 requests and emit `microbatch.prefetch_overlap_count`.

devon: Will add sampling and increase canary to 5% after 10m if p95 delta < +4ms and kv_hit_rate trending up.

paul: Also let's record kernel-selection logs for canary only: `KERNEL=opt-mem-prefetch-v2` and `microbatch.size` in structured logs. Helps correlate.

perf-bot: Canary metrics (10m snapshot): p95 +3.9ms, microbatch size +0.2, kv_hit_rate +4%. Continue to 5%? :thumbsup:

anya: 👍 proceed to 5% but keep 1m alert windows. If p95 creeps > +8ms at any point, auto-revert.

rachel: Post-mortem TODOs if this recurs: (1) add unit test for prefetch vs coalescing, (2) add perf regression gate to kernel merge PRs, (3) create a quick rollback playbook.

paul: I'll draft the rollback playbook and the test cases. Thanks team — let's reconvene after 30m of 5% canary.
